case.pattern_description: One device profile (None) makes low-value online purchases on many unrelated customers' cards, always marked New to the account and behind an anonymous proxy, keeping amounts small so the model scores them low. It touched 2 other cards around this alert and matches earlier confirmed cases on the same profile. It was found by pivoting from the card to the device profile and grouping every card on it.

sar.narrative: This report concerns customer C11663, card C11663-K1, issued as a mastercard debit. Between 2017-01-22 and 2017-01-31, 7 transaction(s) totalling $8,551.47 were identified as part of one fraud episode, beginning with transaction 3660147. The activity took place online, product code(s) C, billing region(s) 315, 327. The transactions were online purchases of one product stepping up roughly doubling in amount until they reached a fixed cap, the same ladder appearing on other customers' cards. The activity is assessed as an undocumented coordinated pattern: The same ladder capped at $1,800.00 appears on 2 other cards within 14 days: coordinated cash-out across customers; Amount ladder on card C11663-K1: 7 online product C purchases from $181.73 up to $1,800.00 within 9.2 days: a stepped cash-out probing the limit. The shared element (a repeated amount ladder capped at $1,800.00 (product C)) links this activity to 2 other card(s), including C08563-K1, C08943-K2, which indicates a common actor across cardholders. Earlier confirmed cases CC-3748, CC-3841, CC-4124 show the same pattern. The cardholder reported the disputed transaction to the bank and denied making it. The bank has recommended BLOCK_CARD, MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS and opened an internal case; the report is filed under R9, §3a.

stop_reason: Fraud probability 0.94 is at or above 0.85 with 3 independent evidence groups (sequence, network, customer), so section 6 allows a decision without asking the customer; further queries would not change the actions.
